outcome: Presence of inflammation and anaphylactoid reaction in the uterine isthmus
Numbers of tryptase-positive degranulating mast cells, elastase-positive neutrophils, CD68-positive macrophages, and C5aR-positive cells in the isthmus
cohort: Women who underwent cesarean hysterectomy for refractory postpartum hemorrhage of unknown etiology between 2011 and 2017 in Japan
finding: Inflammation and an anaphylactoid reaction were histologically detected in the uterine isthmus of women with PAM in the uterine body, suggesting that the isthmus may also be involved in the pathophysiology of refractory uterine atony.
